right_type_wrong_parameters.source_quote: Subsistence while away overnight on District business is reimbursable up to forty dollars ($40.00) per person per day for meals and one hundred fifty dollars ($150.00) per night for lodging.
Counsel shall furnish a receipt for every cost item in excess of $20.00.

missed.source_quote: the aggregate of all fees and costs invoiced on a matter shall at no time surpass the maximum compensation set out in the applicable engagement letter unless and until the Board has approved an increase by written amendment.

Where the engagement letter divides the maximum compensation among phases of work, Counsel shall not invoice against any phase a sum greater than the portion assigned to that phase, it being understood that savings in one phase do not carry over to another without the General Manager's written consent.
Hourly rates are those appearing in the fee schedule attached to the engagement letter, and no timekeeper shall be billed at a rate higher than the rate there shown for that timekeeper.
The District will not pay for the time of any person who does not appear by name in the fee schedule.
Absent the General Manager's prior written consent, not more than four (4) timekeepers shall record time to a single matter in any one billing month.
All time shall be kept contemporaneously and stated in units of one-tenth (0.1) of an hour.

Each entry shall be confined to one activity; an entry exceeding one and one-half (1.5) hours that aggregates distinct activities under a single time figure will be disallowed in its entirety, the District being unable to assess the reasonableness of the time devoted to each.
Time submitted more than one hundred twenty (120) days after the date on which the work was performed is deemed waived.
Counsel shall review each invoice before submission to ensure that no service appears on it more than once; any repeated entry will be deducted.
Time spent in transit is compensable only where the General Counsel has authorized the trip in writing before it is taken; authorized transit time is paid at the timekeeper's ordinary rate.
The hourly rates are understood to absorb the cost of secretarial support, filing, photocopying, calendaring and similar administrative functions, none of which shall appear as a time charge.
Costs advanced to third parties on the District's behalf shall be invoiced in the amount actually paid, without surcharge or handling fee.

missed.source_quote: Quarter-hour increments (0.25) are fine with us, just be consistent about it.
Please don't cram a whole afternoon into one line: two related tasks in an entry is OK, but if an entry of more than an hour lists three or more things I'll send it back to be split.
Tell me what you actually did, because "work on matter" or "review file" tells me nothing and I can't approve it.
For hearings and depositions, two of your lawyers at most on our dime.
Internal meetings among your own team: bill up to half an hour (0.5) per entry and no more.
Clear it with me before the team spends more than 6 hours on legal research on a matter.
Anything older than 60 days when the bill goes out, we won't pay.
If a line shows up twice, we pay it once.
Please don't pass through overhead: online research subscriptions, phones, postage, staff overtime, word processing.
put "(GenAI)" in the narrative of any time entry where one was used.
We won't pay lawyer rates for AI-written summaries or digests of depositions and documents, or for AI doing the first-level document review.
